reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm estrogen receptor engagement by either tamoxifen or raloxifene. Both compounds are known SERMs but target engagement was not measured in this cognitive study. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers measured to confirm estrogen signaling modulation. The trial assumed mechanism engagement based on known pharmacology but did not verify it. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both arms showed negative effect sizes on cognitive endpoints (BVRT: tamoxifen -0.73 vs raloxifene -1.41 errors; CVLT: tamoxifen -3.31 vs raloxifene -1.89). No p-values reported but negative effect sizes suggest cognitive decline rather than improvement. The head-to-head comparison showed raloxifene performed slightly better than tamoxifen but both were associated with cognitive decline. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Mixed subgroup results across different cognitive subtests, but overall pattern suggests neither SERM provided cognitive benefit in postmenopausal women. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a large study (N=1498) with adequate duration (5 years treatment, 3 years cognitive assessment), so underpowering is unlikely. The failure appears to be that estrogen receptor modulation did not translate to cognitive benefit in this population.
